newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FULL STATEMENT BY CZECH CBANK ON CZK INTERVENTION.
newsitem.headline: FULL STATEMENT BY CZECH CBANK ON CZK INTERVENTION.

text.p: The following is an unofficial translation of a statement issued by the Czech National Bank after it had intervened to support the crown early on Thursday morning:

"The Czech National Bank (CNB) intervened on the foreign exchange market today with the aim of stabilising the exchange rate of the crown. Its tendency to weaken was caused in recent days by fluctuations of some foreign currencies whose influence began to filter into the trading in the crown.
A weakening of the crown caused by this could, in the short term, negatively influence the crown financial market.
The last time the CNB intervened on the foreign exchange market was in February 1996 after the widening of the fluctuation band.

Also back then the sucessful interventions resisted a short-term weakening of the exchange rate of the crown, which was technical in character, and connected with market uncertainity and was not in a direct relation with the indicators of the economic development in the Czech Republic.
In case of need the CNB is ready for further interventions."
